messages.content:
You are assisting with business process modelling. Check whether the statements in the list below hold for the business process described below.

INSTRUCTIONS
- For each statement, choose its status using ONLY the process description:
  - "confirmed": the description states that it holds, in the same or different words.
  - "contradicted": the description states something that makes it false.
  - "not_stated": the description does not say whether it holds.
- Do not guess facts the description does not state. If in doubt, use "not_stated".
- A statement that the organisation handles personal data on behalf of another organisation is "confirmed" only if the quoted words show that another organisation decides why and how the data is used (see the ROLE DEFINITIONS below). A word that only looks like a role (for example "processing" or "processed" for a processor) never confirms it; then use "not_stated".
- quote: for "confirmed" or "contradicted", copy the words of the process description that show it, exactly and word for word. For "not_stated", use null. Quotes are checked automatically; a quote that does not appear in the description counts as "not_stated".
- Give one result for every statement, with its id, and no other results.
- Answer with one JSON object that follows the JSON schema below. Output only the JSON, with no other text.

ROLE DEFINITIONS (fixed, the same for every process)
- controller: an organisation that decides why and how personal data is used, for its own purposes.
- processor: an organisation that handles personal data on behalf of another organisation, which decides why and how the data is used.

EXAMPLE (made up, for the format only)
Statements: "C1: a customer pays by card", "C2: the organisation handles personal data on behalf of another organisation", "E1: the customer declines the receipt"
Process: "The customer chooses a product. The customer pays by card and the payment is processed. The shop sends the product."
Answer: {"results": [{"id": "C1", "status": "confirmed", "quote": "The customer pays by card"}, {"id": "C2", "status": "not_stated", "quote": null}, {"id": "E1", "status": "not_stated", "quote": null}]}

JSON SCHEMA
{
  "$defs": {
    "ItemCheck": {
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "description": "The id of the item, as given in the list",
          "title": "Id",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "status": {
          "description": "confirmed, contradicted or not_stated, judged from the description only",
          "enum": [
            "confirmed",
            "not_stated",
            "contradicted"
          ],
          "title": "Status",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "quote": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Exact words copied from the process description, or null for not_stated",
          "title": "Quote"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "id",
        "status",
        "quote"
      ],
      "title": "ItemCheck",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "properties": {
    "results": {
      "description": "One result for every item of the list",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/ItemCheck"
      },
      "title": "Results",
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "results"
  ],
  "title": "CheckOutputV2",
  "type": "object"
}

PROCESS DESCRIPTION
An e-commerce company has a comprehensive order fulfillment process:
When a customer places an order, the system records the order details.
Payment processing begins.
If the payment fails, the customer is notified, and the process ends.
Upon successful payment, the inventory system checks stock availability.
If items are out of stock, a back-order is initiated, and the customer is informed about the delay.
The process continues once the back-order is received and all required items are available in stock.
In-stock items are picked from the warehouse.
Quality control checks are performed on the picked items.
Packaging is done, including gift wrapping if the customer requested it.
Meanwhile, the shipping department prepares shipping documents and labels.
If the order is international, customs documentation is prepared.
Once packaging and shipping documents are ready, the order is dispatched.
The system sends a shipping confirmation to the customer.
After dispatch, the system updates the inventory levels.
A follow-up email for feedback is sent directly after confirming the successful delivery.
If the customer reports any issues upon delivery, a returns process is initiated, which includes:
Sending a return shipping label.
Receiving returned items.
Inspecting returned items.
Processing a refund or replacement.

STATEMENTS
S1: the buyer is a consumer (a natural person acting for purposes which are outside that person's trade, business, craft or profession)
T1: the organisation running the described process sells goods or services to customers, for purposes relating to its trade, business, craft or profession
C1: the consumer has communicated his decision to withdraw from the contract to the trader in accordance with Article 11
C2: the trader has not offered to collect the goods himself
C3: the contract is an off-premises contract
C4: the goods have been delivered to the consumer’s home at the time of the conclusion of the contract
C5: by their nature, those goods cannot normally be returned by post
E1: the trader has offered to collect the goods himself
E2: the trader has agreed to bear the direct cost of returning the goods
E3: the trader failed to inform the consumer that the consumer has to bear the direct cost of returning the goods
